subject: chemistry
title: Reaction profiles and activation energy
key_idea: Particles react only if they collide with enough energy. The minimum energy needed is the activation energy. A reaction profile shows the energy of the reactants and products, the activation energy and the overall energy change.

blocks.text: This section covers why particles need a minimum energy before they can react.

items.meaning: The minimum energy that particles must have to react.
A diagram showing how the energy changes as reactants turn into products.

items: Chemical reactions can occur only when reacting particles **collide** with each other.
The particles must also collide with enough energy. This minimum energy is the **activation energy**.
If the particles have less energy than the activation energy, they still collide but the collisions are not successful.
A mixture of methane and oxygen does not react at room temperature. The particles collide, but have less energy than the activation energy.
Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for particles to react.
Collisions with less energy than this do not lead to a reaction.

blocks.text: A reaction profile is a curved line. It shows the energy of the particles as the reaction proceeds.

items.text: Label the vertical axis energy and the horizontal axis progress of reaction.
Draw a level line at the start and label it reactants.
Draw a curve up to a peak, then down to a second level line labelled products.
Draw an arrow from the reactants level up to the top of the peak and label it activation energy.
Draw an arrow between the reactants level and the products level and label it overall energy change.

diagram.alt: Pick exothermic or endothermic to see its reaction profile.
result_labels: Energy of products compared with reactants

options.label: Exothermic
results: Energy is transferred to the surroundings

options.label: Endothermic
results: Energy is taken in from the surroundings

items: In both types, the curve rises first. Energy must be put in to reach the peak, so activation energy is always shown as an upward arrow.
If the products are **lower** than the reactants, the reaction is exothermic.
If the products are **higher** than the reactants, the reaction is endothermic.
(Higher tier) In an exothermic reaction, the energy released making bonds is greater than the energy taken in breaking bonds.
Label reactants, products, activation energy and overall energy change.
Products lower than reactants means exothermic. Products higher means endothermic.

checks.q: What is meant by activation energy?
checks.a: The minimum energy that particles must have to react (needed for a reaction to occur).

checks.q: A reaction profile shows the products at a lower energy than the reactants. State the type of reaction and what happens to the temperature of the surroundings.
checks.a: Exothermic. The temperature of the surroundings increases.

checks.q: Which labelled arrow on a reaction profile shows the activation energy?
checks.a: The arrow from the level of the reactants up to the top of the peak.

exam_phrases: the (minimum) energy needed for particles to react
the (minimum) energy needed for a reaction to occur
the (minimum) energy needed to start a reaction
particles collide but have insufficient energy
energy less than the activation energy (so collisions are not successful)
in an exothermic reaction the energy of the products is lower than the energy of the reactants

mistakes.wrong: At room temperature the methane and oxygen particles do not collide.
mistakes.right: The particles collide, but they have insufficient energy, less than the activation energy, so the collisions are not successful.

mistakes.wrong: In an exothermic reaction the energy of the products is higher than the energy of the reactants.
mistakes.right: In an exothermic reaction the energy of the products is lower than the energy of the reactants.

worked_example.question:
Methane, ethane, propane and butane all react with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water.

Suggest why a mixture of methane and oxygen does not react at room temperature.

Answer in terms of particles.
answer_points: But at room temperature the particles have insufficient energy, or have less energy than the activation energy, so the collisions are not successful.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the collision and one mark for the energy being below the activation energy.

exam_phrases: energy is taken in breaking bonds (in the reactants)
energy is given out making bonds (in the products)
more energy is given out than taken in

mistakes.wrong: The reaction profile shows that the products have less energy than the reactants.
mistakes.right: This alone is ignored. Describe the energy in bond breaking and bond making, and say more energy is given out than taken in.

mistakes.wrong: The reaction is exothermic because more bonds are made than broken.
mistakes.right: References to the number of bonds are ignored. Compare the energy: more energy is released forming bonds than is needed to break bonds.

exam_phrases: energy required to start the reaction
energy required for a successful collision to occur
the (minimum) amount of energy needed for a reaction to start or occur
the (minimum) amount of energy for a successful collision

mistakes.wrong: Activation energy is the energy needed to activate the reaction.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say it is the (minimum) energy needed to start the reaction, or for a successful collision to occur.

worked_example.question:
A student draws the reaction profile for a reaction.

Explain what is meant by the term activation energy.
answer_points: The energy required to start the reaction, or the energy required for a successful collision to occur.
worked_example.tip: Use the words start the reaction or successful collision.
